interface.name: dde_xwayland_coordinate_manager_v1

description.summary: map owned surfaces into the local Xwayland root

interface.description: Experimental interoperability protocol, not a wayland-protocols standard. This protocol maps surface-local rectangles to the compositor's local Xwayland root coordinate space. It does not expose toolkit DPI, physical output pixels, input method state, or other clients' surfaces.

interface.name: dde_xwayland_coordinate_v1

description.summary: a live surface-local to X root mapping

interface.description:
The object tracks a rectangle on one surface. Coordinates supplied by the client are surface-local, after toolkit-to-surface conversion, not buffer pixels. Neither buffer_scale nor the preferred fractional rendering scale is to be applied by the client.
Replies are asynchronous. A new rectangle supersedes the previous one. The compositor also republishes the last rectangle when the surface moves or the Xwayland mapping changes. Clients must discard results for obsolete serials and destroy the object when its input context loses focus.
The compositor supplies the local X display name and root XID in every mapped event. Results may only be used with that X server. A new generation is emitted for each result; clients must not combine fields from different results. When the surface is unmapped, destroyed, or Xwayland is unavailable, unavailable invalidates the last result. The object survives unmapping but cannot be rebound to a different wl_surface.
After unavailable the compositor resumes mapped events when the mapping becomes available again, without requiring another set_rectangle request. Results are coordinate conversions, not popup placement decisions: they are not clipped to the surface or to output boundaries. Zero-width or zero-height rectangles are valid. Each component is rounded to the nearest native integer pixel, with half-way values rounded away from zero.
